contract.reader: A student or engineer who has the state-space form from the primer and basic linear algebra, and is about to design a controller
contract.problem: Why the eigenvalues of A decide whether a linear system decays, oscillates or grows, what else they say about the response, and when they are not enough
contract.outcome: Write the free response as a sum of modes; read decay rate, frequency, natural frequency and damping ratio from an eigenvalue; classify marginal and repeated cases; recognize transient growth and hidden unstable modes; apply the unit-circle test and the Euler step-size condition; judge local stability of a nonlinear equilibrium from its Jacobian
contract.contribution: One running example (the primer's mass-spring-damper) through modes, damping, transfer function and discrete time with numerical checks, plus three counterexamples (double integrator, non-normal matrix, hidden mode) that show the limits of the eigenvalue test
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; three NumPy scripts with their output; Astrom and Murray (2021), Chen (2013), Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini (2019), Khalil (2002), Trefethen and Embree (2005)
contract.limitations: Modal proof assumes a diagonalizable matrix (Jordan case stated, not proved); no Lyapunov direct method, pseudospectra or formal controllability/observability tests (the controllability test is in the next entry)
